mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best describes the correct understanding of force?

options.A: Force is a push or pull that only acts on objects already in motion.
options.B: Force is a push or pull that can act on any object, whether at rest or moving.
options.C: Force is a property of an object that depends only on its mass.
options.D: Force is the same as weight and always acts upward.

mcqs.answer: Force is a push or pull that can act on any object, whether at rest or moving.
mcqs.explanation: Force is an interaction that can change the state of motion of any object, whether it is at rest or moving (Newton's First Law). Option A is a common misconception; forces do not require prior motion. Options C and D describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: A book rests on a table while a car accelerates on a straight road. Which statement correctly identifies the type of forces acting in each case?

options.B: The book experiences balanced forces; the car experiences unbalanced forces.
options.C: The book experiences unbalanced forces; the car experiences balanced forces.

mcqs.answer: The book experiences balanced forces; the car experiences unbalanced forces.
mcqs.explanation: The book is at rest, so its weight is balanced by the normal reaction – net force zero (balanced). The accelerating car has a net forward force greater than the opposing forces, so the forces are unbalanced. Options A, C, and D misclassify the situations.

mcqs.question: Two objects, A and B, each experience a force of 10 N. Object A receives the force horizontally, while object B receives the same magnitude vertically upward. Which statement correctly compares the effects of these forces?

options.A: Both objects will have the same change in speed because the magnitude of force is the same.
options.B: Object A will move faster than B because horizontal forces are more effective.
options.C: Both objects will experience the same magnitude of acceleration, but their motion directions will differ.
options.D: Object B will not accelerate because upward forces are opposed by gravity.

mcqs.answer: Both objects will experience the same magnitude of acceleration, but their motion directions will differ.
mcqs.explanation: Acceleration = Force/mass; with equal forces and equal masses, the magnitude of acceleration is the same. The direction of motion follows the direction of the applied force, so A moves horizontally and B moves vertically. Option A ignores direction, B is incorrect, and D misinterprets gravity's role.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise force as a vector quantity at a basic level
mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly represents a force vector acting on a body?
mcqs.explanation: A vector must specify both magnitude and direction. Option B gives a clear magnitude (15 N) and a direction (east). Option A and C are scalars lacking direction, while option D, though technically a component representation, is unnecessarily complex for a basic vector description.

mcqs.question: In physics, what is meant by the term 'force'?

options.A: A property of matter that determines its inertia.
options.B: An interaction that can change the state of motion of an object.
options.C: The amount of matter in an object.

mcqs.answer: An interaction that can change the state of motion of an object.
mcqs.explanation: Force is defined as an interaction that can cause a change in the motion (speed or direction) of an object. Options A and C describe mass, while D describes speed, none of which define force.

mcqs.question: Which situation illustrates balanced forces acting on an object?

options.A: A soccer ball rolling and gradually stopping.
options.B: A book lying motionless on a table.
options.C: A car accelerating on a highway.
options.D: A skydiver falling with an open parachute.

mcqs.answer: A book lying motionless on a table.
mcqs.explanation: The book is at rest with its weight balanced by the normal reaction from the table, resulting in zero net force (balanced). The other options involve net unbalanced forces causing motion changes.

mcqs.question: How does a force affect an object's speed compared to its direction?

options.A: A force can change speed but never direction.
options.B: A force can change direction but never speed.
options.C: A force can change both speed and direction depending on its line of action.
options.D: A force always changes both speed and direction equally.

mcqs.answer: A force can change both speed and direction depending on its line of action.
mcqs.explanation: If the force is applied along the line of motion, it changes speed (magnitude of velocity). If applied at an angle, it can also change direction. Thus, both speed and direction can be affected, but not necessarily both at the same time. Options A, B, and D are overly restrictive or inaccurate.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise force as a vector quantity at a basic level
mcqs.question: A child pushes a toy car with a force of 5 N to the right. Simultaneously, a wind exerts a force of 3 N to the left on the same car. What is the net force acting on the car?
mcqs.explanation: Net force = 5 N (right) – 3 N (left) = 2 N to the right. This demonstrates vector addition where opposite directions subtract. Options A and D incorrectly add magnitudes, while C reverses the direction.
